summary: The tab bar scrolls when the tabs don't fit, and + stays in the bar. src/finder/tab_bar.rs, `render_tab_bar`: the tabs sit in a strip `tabs` (`flex_1().min_w_0().max_w(n tabs at their widest).overflow_x_scroll().track_scroll(..)`), with `new-tab` after it as the bar's next child. Two constants, TAB_MAX_WIDTH and TAB_GAP, give both the tab's cap and the strip's. The bar ends with an `on_prepaint` that compares where the strip was drawn last (`scroll.bounds()`, read while rendering) with where this frame put it; when they differ it asks for the tab that shows again (`scroll_to_item(active)`) and for one more frame (`request_animation_frame`). A tab's context-menu builder starts with a window-bounds observer that closes the menu when the window's size changes while the menu has the keyboard, the remedy `history_menu` uses. src/workspace.rs: `tab_scroll: ScrollHandle` with a getter; `new_tab`, `select_tab`, and `close_tab` when the closed tab was the one showing call `scroll_to_item(self.active)`; `move_tab` and closing a background tab don't. docs/manual.md: three sentences in the Tabs paragraph and the tests/basics.rs line. tests/basics.rs: nine tests and four helpers beside the other tab tests.
changelog: With more tabs than fit, the last tabs and the + button ran off the right edge of the window, or under the second pane in split view, where the mouse couldn't reach them. The tab bar now scrolls sideways: turn the mouse wheel or swipe over the tabs to see the rest. A tab you open or switch to scrolls into view, the tab that shows stays in view when the window changes size or split view is turned on, and + stays at the end of the bar. A tab's right-click menu closes when the window changes size, where it used to go out of sight and come back later with only a click to close it.
behaviour_changes: With more tabs than fit, the tabs scroll sideways inside the tab bar instead of being laid out past the pane's right edge. Tabs out of view are cut off at the strip's two edges, 10pt inside the bar on the left and 6pt before the + on the right. Tested, pictured.
The + stays at the end of the bar, visible and clickable, in split view too. With room to spare it still follows the last tab. Tested, pictured.

New: a mouse wheel turned up or down over the tabs, or a sideways swipe, scrolls them. Before, the wheel did nothing there. With tabs that fit, nothing moves (probed in review: the offset is back at 0 by the next frame). While a tab's right-click menu is open the wheel does nothing: the kit's menu layer takes it (the implementer's probe; read in the kit in review).

A tab that is opened or switched to scrolls into view: Cmd+T, the +, Open in New Tab, a click on a tab, Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab with wrap-around. Tested. A click on the visible sliver of a tab cut off at the strip's edge shows that tab and brings it in whole (probed in review).
Closing the tab that shows (Cmd+W or its ×) scrolls the bar to the tab that takes over. Tested.

Closing a tab that isn't showing (its × or its menu) and dragging a tab to another place leave the bar where it is. Tested for the close. Probed in review: with the bar at its far end, three closes of the last tab in a row each put the next last tab under the same point, and a tab dragged onto another in a scrolled strip changes places with the strip left alone.

From the review: the tab that shows comes back into view whenever the bar's room changes: split view turned on or off, the window made narrower or wider, the sidebar hidden, shown or dragged, the text size changed. Also when the bar had been scrolled away from that tab by hand: the wheel leaves the bar where you put it only until its room changes (probed for the sidebar and a wider window, and pictured for the wheel in split view). The implementer's commit left the tab out of view in these cases, as the plan of record accepted. Tested for split view and a narrower window, pictured for split view.

From the review: a tab bar that comes back scrolls from where it is now. A bar goes when the second-last tab closes; when the next one had less room (split view turned on meanwhile) and several folders were opened in tabs at once, the tab that shows ended out of view, 117pt past the strip's end in the probe. Tested.

Several folders opened in tabs at once from a one-tab window end with the last tab in view. A frame that draws the strip somewhere else than the frame before asks for one extra frame, and no other frame does (probed: once the callbacks left by earlier steps had run, round after round of the window's next frame found none pending, with ten tabs, in split view, and in a pane too narrow for any tab). Tested with the frame request pinned.

From the review: a tab's right-click menu closes when the window changes size, as the Back and Forward buttons' menus do, and the keyboard goes back to where it was. Before, on the trunk with focus-lost-recovery: when the tab moved from under the pressed point the files got the keyboard, the menu stayed open out of sight, and it was drawn again, without the keyboard, when the tab was back there; Escape didn't close it, a click did. A window with a few tabs had this too, since its tabs change width with it (probed without the observer: five tabs at 850pt, a menu on the fourth, 760pt and back). On the code before this change and before focus-lost-recovery the same resize left every key dead until a click (probed). A window that only moves or comes to the front leaves the menu open. Tested.

When the tabs fit, nothing changes: every tab and the + are at the same positions as before for 2 to 9 tabs at 1100pt and 11 tabs at 1600pt and 3000pt (the implementer's measurements on both versions; my own 3-tab picture matches theirs).

docs/manual.md says the above in the Tabs paragraph: the bar scrolls, the wheel and a swipe, a tab opened or switched to scrolls into view and so does the tab that shows when the bar gets wider or narrower, and + stays at the end.
left_out: No cue that more tabs exist beyond the tab cut off at the strip's edge. The brief says a fade or chevron could follow later.
No auto-scroll while a tab is dragged to the strip's edge (the brief's risk, accepted): a tab can't be dragged onto one that is out of view.

A tab's menu is closed only by a change of the window's size. Whatever else moves its tab from under the pressed point leaves the menu open as far as the kit knows, as for every context menu on the trunk (see the focus-lost-recovery record). Probed on the trunk commit: ten tabs, a menu on a tab, Cmd+Alt+S twice: the files have the keyboard and the menu is drawn again without it; Escape doesn't close it, Cmd+T works. Split view turned on with a tab's menu open: the new pane's files have the keyboard and the menu isn't drawn.

A tab closed or dragged away from the left of the tab that shows moves that tab one place to the left, which can take it under the strip's left edge. The bar stays where the mouse is working, by the rule above. The plan of record's single reveal in `tabs_changed` would have brought it back, and would also throw the bar back to the showing tab after every close of a background tab at the far end. From reading; not probed.

`.flex_shrink_0()` on `new-tab` (in the plan): it does nothing. The + keeps its 22 points down to a 300pt split window where the strip is 0 wide (the implementer's probe, and mine: + at 156..178 with the strip at 150..150).
The optional 56pt minimum tab width (the verifier says skip).

review_fixes: A bug in what the implementer added for the bar's first frame. The strip scrolls to a tab from where it was drawn the frame before, so a bar's first frame has to ask again; the implementer recognised that frame by `tab_scroll.children_count() == 0`, which is true once in a window's life. A bar that had gone (back to one tab) and came back kept its old place in the handle, and a tab asked for was scrolled to from there. Reproduced on 2bbbcb7: two tabs at 1100pt, one closed, split view on, six folders opened in tabs at once: the tab that shows at x=628..708 where the strip ends at 511.5, and it stayed there until a tab was switched. The implementer had listed this as rare and not handled; split view after any earlier use of tabs is enough. Fix in `render_tab_bar`: the prepaint listener is always there and asks again whenever the strip isn't where it was drawn last. Test a_tab_bar_that_comes_back_scrolls_to_the_tab_that_shows.

The plan forbade a `scroll_to_item` in `toggle_split` because it would be worked out from the pre-split width; asked for from the bar's own prepaint, after the strip is laid out, it is worked out from the new one. Test the_tab_that_shows_stays_in_view_when_the_tab_bar_has_less_room; the two after-split pictures retaken from the trunk commit.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code and the probes say. (1) The tab that shows ends up out of view, and the bar no longer says where you are. `scroll_to_item` is worked out in the strip's prepaint from the bounds the handle recorded the frame before, with this frame's child bounds. So it is right when the strip is where it was, and wrong or stale when it isn't: a first frame (no bounds yet, and the request is used up without scrolling), a returning bar (old bounds), a frame in which the room changed. The listener at the end of `render_tab_bar` covers all three with one comparison, and asks for the frame itself, because a notify while drawing waits for the next event (the toolbar and the icon grid do the same). It cannot loop: the strip's bounds don't depend on the scroll offset, and a frame that draws the strip where it was asks for nothing. The tab bar's width is the same for every tab (the sidebar's width and visibility are shared settings), so a tab switch is not a change of room. Left: a tab moved or closed away from the left of the showing one (left_out). (2) The mouse on a scrolled strip: a tab cut off at the edge taking a press meant for the +, a press landing on the wrong tab, a menu or a drag in the wrong place. gpui stores the content mask with each hitbox, so a tab takes presses only where it is drawn; the + is outside the strip. A tab's menu is drawn from the tab's own bounds, which the strip's scrolling moves with it. Probed as above. (3) The keyboard and the frame loop: a wheel over the bar stealing a scroll, keys going dead after tabs move under an open menu, frames asked for without end. The strip's wheel listener acts only while the mouse is over the strip, and nothing scrollable is under it. For the menu see review_fixes and left_out. Idle frames probed.

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) Nothing ran on macOS or Windows. On a Mac check once: a two-finger swipe over the tabs scrolls them the way you expect, sideways and up or down; with six or more tabs, Cmd+Backslash keeps the tab that shows in view; a right-click on a tab and then a drag of the window's edge closes the menu. (b) The bar comes back to the tab that shows on every change of its room, also after you scrolled away from it to look at other tabs. That goes past the plan of record, which accepted the opposite, and I chose the simple rule. If it should hold only while that tab was in view before, the listener at the end of `render_tab_bar` is the one place. (c) Which changes scroll the bar is the implementer's call against the plan (a switch does; a background close and a drag don't), and I kept it: the close test fails with the plan's version. Its price is in left_out. (d) A tab's menu closes on any change of the window's size, also when its tab would have stayed put (a few tabs at their widest), like the history menus. (e) In a frame that changes the bar's room the tab that shows is drawn where it was and scrolls in the next frame, so while a window is dragged narrower its edge is a frame ahead of the tab.

How this meets focus-lost-recovery (4e5b448), which landed while I reviewed. Its net gives the files the keyboard when a menu stops being drawn. The observer here closes a tab's menu before that can happen on a resize, so the net is not needed there and no menu is left open out of sight. Where the window keeps its size the net acts and the kit's menu stays open unseen (left_out). The browser's new listener for presses on what takes no keys runs for a press on a tab or on the bar's empty part as for any other; a click on a tab still ends with that tab's files holding the keyboard (the tab tests click tabs, their close buttons and the +), and the wheel is not a press.

For briefs still to come.
- tab-drop-and-close: read `git show 7e5689c` before you plan. The bar `tab-bar` now has three children: the strip `tabs`, `new-tab`, and the canvas `on_prepaint` adds. The strip's children must be exactly the tabs, in order, because `scroll_to_item` goes by child index: wrapping a tab (folder_drop_target, the context menu) is fine, a sibling inside the strip is not; put anything else in the bar, before the `on_prepaint`. A tab's menu builder is now `move |menu, window, cx|` and starts with the observer that closes it when the window changes size: add Close Other Tabs after it. a_tabs_menu_closes_when_the_window_changes_size compares the menu's labels with ["Close Tab", "Move Tab to New Window"], so add yours to its `menu`. A middle-click close through `close_tab` scrolls the bar only when the showing tab was closed, which is right for closes in a row with the mouse in place. `close_other_tabs` leaves one tab and no bar, so it needs no scroll call; a new Workspace function that changes which tab shows calls `self.tab_scroll.scroll_to_item(self.active)` as `select_tab` does. Hitboxes are clipped by the strip: a tab that is cut off takes a drop or a middle-click only on the part that shows, and a tab out of view takes none; a drag doesn't scroll the strip. TAB_MAX_WIDTH and TAB_GAP are constants now. The tab IDs are unchanged. Helpers for your tests are listed under tests.
- restore-session-tabs: `Workspace` has a field `tab_scroll: ScrollHandle`; a constructor shared with `new` has to set it (`ScrollHandle::new()`). A restored window needs no scroll call: the bar's first frame finds its strip somewhere it was not drawn before and asks for `active_index()` itself, for the next frame.
- split-active-pane: `toggle_split` needs no scroll call and should get none: one there would be worked out from the width before the split, and the bar's own prepaint does it from the new width. The bar belongs to the first pane only, so `tabs`, `tab-bar`, `new-tab` and ("tab", ix) are not repeated in split view. Ctrl+Tab pressed with the keyboard in the other pane switches the first pane's tab (seen in a probe), and `select_tab` then gives that tab's files the keyboard (from reading), so the active pane changes with it. `Workspace` has one new field and three new lines in `new_tab`, `select_tab` and `close_tab`; its `render` is as it was.
- split-view-toolbar-clip: when split view narrows the sidebar, the bar's strip moves and grows, and the bar brings its showing tab back by itself. The tests' sums hold with your numbers: at 1100pt split with a 175.5pt sidebar the strip has 326pt, where three tabs fit and five, seven and eight don't (the_new_tab_button_stays_in_its_pane_in_split_view, a_tab_bar_that_comes_back_scrolls_to_the_tab_that_shows, the_tab_that_shows_stays_in_view_when_the_tab_bar_has_less_room, whose comment says split view holds three). more_tabs_than_fit is a single pane at 850pt with the sidebar at 212pt (590pt for tabs that want 854). Below about 48pt of room beside the sidebar the + runs out of the bar, which only a window under the minimum reaches today (probed at 300pt split).
- recent-searches: the remedy at the top of `history_menu` now has a second copy, at the top of a tab's menu in tab_bar.rs. A third would be the time to share one function. Each copy's test also pins its focus check: without it a menu that was closed by hand would send Cancel to whatever has the keyboard at the next resize (here it closed a dialog; in tests/controls.rs it closes the other history menu).
- context-menus-fit: a tab's menu is two short items and has the observer described above; nothing to fit.
- go-to-folder-keyboard: a_tabs_menu_closes_when_the_window_changes_size opens Go to Folder with Cmd+Shift+G, expects `ui.dialog_open()` after a resize, and closes it with `ui.close_dialog()`. It reads nothing in the dialog.
- idle-redraw-after-search: the tab bar asks for a frame only in a frame that drew its strip somewhere else than the frame before: once when a bar appears, once per change of its room. A wheel event over tabs that fit changes the offset and notifies the view once; the clamp puts it back in the frame that follows.
